system:
You assess whether a hospital's own policies satisfy an accreditation requirement. You are shown the requirement and a numbered list of candidate policy provisions retrieved from the hospital's policy library.

Judge only what the provisions actually say. A provision that shares vocabulary with the requirement but addresses a different obligation does not satisfy it. A provision that satisfies the requirement in different words does satisfy it.

Answer NOT_COVERED only if none of the provisions addresses the requirement. Prefer PARTIAL when something related is present but incomplete: overstating a gap is worse than reporting one cautiously.
prompt:
REQUIREMENT [LD.13.01.01 EP 7]:
The hospital maintains the following:
- Records of the source and disposition of all units of blood and blood components for at least 10 years from the date of disposition in a manner that permits prompt retrieval
- A fully funded plan to transfer these records to another hospital or other entity if the hospital ceases operation for any reason

**Attributes:** Documentation

**Crosswalk:** §482.27(b)(5)(ii), §482.27(b)(5)(ii), §482.27(b)(5)(i), §482.27(b)(5)(i)

CANDIDATE POLICY PROVISIONS:
[C1] Blood Product Transfusion Reaction DETAILED §8 Document in the Medical Record
Document in the Medical Record
Complete nursing documentation must include: time transfusion began, time reaction noted, vital signs trend
(pre/during/post), symptoms described by the patient and observed, all interventions performed with times,
name and time of physician notification, patient response to treatment, and disposition of blood product.

[C2] Rapid Response Team RRT Policy §4 Documentation Requirements
Documentation Requirements
All RRT activations must be documented including: time of activation, team members present, clinical findings,
interventions performed, and patient disposition. A standardized RRT documentation tool must be used.

[C3] Transfer and Discharge Procedures §3 Transfer Documentation
Transfer Documentation
A copy of the medical record (or relevant portions) must accompany the patient. This includes: vital signs,
assessment findings, treatments provided, labs/imaging, and reason for transfer.

[C4] Transfer and Discharge Procedures §4 Patient Notification & Rights
Patient Notification & Rights
Patients must be informed of: the reason for transfer, the name of the receiving facility, their right to refuse transfer
(with documentation of risks of refusal), and their rights at the receiving facility.

[C5] Informed Consent §4 Special Consent Situations
Special Consent Situations
Separate consents are required for: blood transfusions, HIV testing, release of records, research participation,
photography, and treatment of minors (with appropriate exceptions for emergencies).

[C6] Staffing and Delivery of Care §5 Staffing Variance Documentation
Staffing Variance Documentation
When staffing falls below the approved plan, the variance must be documented including: the reason, the actual
staffing, corrective actions taken, and impact on patient care. Patterns of understaffing must be escalated to
administration.

Reply with exactly these four lines and nothing else:
VERDICT: one of COVERED, PARTIAL, NOT_COVERED
EVIDENCE: candidate ids that support the verdict (e.g. C1, C3), or NONE
MISSING: what the requirement demands that no candidate provides, or NONE
REASON: one sentence citing what the provisions say
